text: **Hint 1:** Consider the properties of mean-centered data. When you center the data, you are essentially shifting the data so that the mean of each feature (except the intercept) is zero. This transformation does not affect the variance or the relationships between the variables.\n\n**Hint 2:** Think about the effect of mean-centering on the linear regression model. The mean-centering process does not change the underlying relationships between the variables, so the fit of the model (and thus the MSE) should remain the same when comparing the original model on the original data to the new model on the centered data.
